rules.text: Increasing L2 cache sets from 1024 to 2048 slightly improves IPC and notably reduces L2 cache misses, especially when a prefetcher like SPP_DEV is active.
If the L2 cache miss rate (L2C_mpki) is at least 30, increasing the L2 cache capacity can reduce misses and improve IPC by accommodating a larger working set.
When the last-level cache experiences a high miss rate, expanding its capacity is crucial for improving data locality and overall performance by reducing off-chip memory accesses.
For workloads with a moderate L2 miss rate (below 15 MPKI), enabling a stream-based L2 prefetcher can proactively fetch data patterns, reducing effective memory latency and improving IPC.

When the LLC experiences very frequent misses (LLC_mpki >= 15), employing an adaptive replacement policy like DRRIP can better utilize cache lines by protecting frequently reused data more effectively than simpler policies.

If the L2 cache miss rate is already very low, disabling prefetchers can prevent cache pollution and potential performance degradation by avoiding speculative data fetches that might evict useful data.

For workloads exhibiting moderate-to-high IPC, optimizing the LLC replacement policy with SRRIP can offer a good balance of performance and stability over basic LRU by giving newly accessed blocks a chance to be reused.
